consequence: Every disagreement in these volumes turns on a Sanskrit form. A claim whose Sanskrit cannot be quoted correctly cannot be re-found by hand, so the OCR route was abandoned in favour of the sacred-texts transcription through the Wayback Machine, which preserves the diacritics and the printed page numbers.
finding: The English prose OCRs adequately. The transliterated Sanskrit does not: krnavama appears as "Kyvzzdvama", pravrddha as "pravrzddha", achantsanta as "A#&santa", chadayatha as "#Aadayatha".
reusable_lesson: For this domain, a proofread transcription beats a scan of the same book, even when the scan is the primary artifact. The scan is better evidence and worse data.
tested: archive.org full-text layers for SBE 32 and SBE 46 (vedichymns01mulluoft, vedichymns02mulluoft), 1.29 MB and 0.81 MB.
